newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore foreign stocks soggy early, OTC's active.
newsitem.headline: Singapore foreign stocks soggy early, OTC's active.

text.p: Singapore foreign shares turned soggy early Monday, hit by renewed liquidation, while Malaysian over-the-counter issues held favour, dealers said.
Changes to the weighting of the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) Singapore Index announced on Friday caused heavy selling in foreign tranches of blue chips stocks.
"Investors are underweighting Singapore blue chips because there will not be that much of a premium in foreign stocks," a dealer with a local brokerage said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was down 10.94 points at 2,230.34.
At 0240 GMT, turnover was a healthy 144 million shares with declining issues outpacing advancers by 190 to 141.
Investors were also in a cautious mood ahead of the results anticipated during the current earnings reporting season.
Dealers said this was triggering better demand for Malaysian stocks and small-capitalised local shares.
Malaysia's paper and property investment company Insas Bhd led the actives with 9.35 million shares traded. The stock hit a new high at Singapore $1.30, up S$0.04.
Foreign losers included the foreign tranches of SPH, DBS, OCBC and UOB banks.
